key_insight: The paper introduces a level-set topology optimization method that controls material volume directly by enforcing a volume-compatible velocity before each transport step, reducing dependence on Lagrange or penalty tuning.
engineering_relevance: This gives a more robust way to satisfy volume constraints in structural and fluid design optimization while maintaining stable objective evolution.
method: Add a scalar weighted volume-compatibility constraint to a modified Stokes-type extension-regularization problem.
Ensure the initial velocity is volume compatible, then evolve the level set over a frozen transport interval.
Provide continuous and DG semi-discrete estimates for regularized-volume drift versus smoothing, mesh size, transport time, and velocity.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on minimum compliance, eigenfrequency maximization, and minimum energy dissipation benchmarks, with theoretical drift bounds and demonstrated effectiveness in all three.
watch_item: Performance depends on the frozen-time interval, smoothing parameter, and spatial discretization, so implementation still requires careful numerical setup.
paper_title: A volume-controlled level-set method for topology optimization
